title: Kerala's Temple Vault Has Been Sealed Since The 1880s

basis.note: median of recent videos blended with the niche benchmark; learning gated until day 5

predicted_range.basis: about 3x either way, from backtested error (249 of our own videos so far)

segments.narration: A temple vault in Kerala has stayed shut since the 1880s. Six chambers sit under Thiruvananthapuram's Padmanabhaswamy temple, labelled simply A to F.
In 2011 India's Supreme Court ordered five of them opened and inventoried. Vault A alone gave up over a hundred thousand objects.
Eight hundred kilos of gold coins, some of them struck around 200 BCE. And the sixth door simply stayed closed.
Not for want of a crowbar. A temple ritual in 2011 declared Vault B a forbidden zone, and the priests have opposed opening it ever since.
The court sided with custom. In July 2020 it handed control back to the former Travancore royal family, and Vault B is still sealed today.

verdicts.claim: The Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram has six known vaults labelled A to F, and Vault B is believed to have been unopened since the 1880s.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia states the temple has six known vaults labelled A to F and that Vault B is believed to be unopened since the 1880s.

verdicts.claim: In 2011 the Supreme Court of India directed that the chambers be opened and inventoried; vaults A, C, D, E and F were opened, and over 1.02 lakh articles were retrieved from Vault A and its antechambers.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia records the June 2011 Supreme Court direction, the opening of vaults A, C, D, E and F with their antechambers, and over 1.02 lakh articles from Vault A and its antechambers.

verdicts.claim: Vault A held a hoard of about 800 kg of gold coins dating to around 200 BCE.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia records an 800 kg hoard of gold coins in Vault A dating to around 200 BCE. No total valuation for the 2011 inventory is cited, and the narration deliberately makes no value claim.

verdicts.claim: A four-day Ashtamangala Devaprasnam ritual in August 2011 declared Vault B a forbidden zone, and opening it has been opposed on religious grounds since.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia records the August 2011 four-day Ashtamangala Devaprasnam declaring Kallara B a forbidden zone and the 8 February 2016 letter from the Naduvil Madhom Pushpanjali Swamiyar opposing its opening.

verdicts.claim: On 13 July 2020 the Supreme Court of India ruled that administration and control of the temple rests with the erstwhile Travancore royal family, and Vault B remains unopened.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia records the 13 July 2020 Supreme Court judgment overturning the Kerala High Court and vesting administration and control in the erstwhile Travancore royal family, and that Vault B remains unopened.

candidates.text: A temple vault in Kerala has stayed shut since the 1880s.
candidates.why: Leads on a specific sealed door and a date, which is its own question.

candidates.text: India's Supreme Court opened five vaults and stopped at the sixth.
candidates.why: Leads on the court stopping short, strong but needs the temple named.

candidates.text: One room held eight hundred kilos of ancient gold coins.
candidates.why: Leads on the treasure, but treasure found closes the loop instead of opening it.

choice.reason: A door nobody has opened in nearly 150 years is the open loop the whole story turns on, where the gold-coins line answers the question in the first breath.
